title: Exact real-valued recovery
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and let $k\ge1$ satisfy that every set in the Fourier support of the real-valued sign representation of $f$ has size at most $k$. For each subset $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\le k$, choose a batch of the prescribed number of inputs, and suppose that for every such $S$ the empirical Fourier coefficient differs from the true Fourier coefficient of $f$ by strictly less than the estimator's accuracy parameter. The real-valued function represented by the estimator's sparse Fourier hypothesis then equals the real-valued sign representation of $f$ at every input.
hypotheses_covered: integer degree parameter k with 1 ≤ k
Fourier degree of the real-valued target is at most k
a batch of the prescribed size for each subset of size at most k
for every such subset, the empirical coefficient error is strictly less than the specified accuracy
